recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-16139; future wording changes to `CodeSystem/referencerange-meaning` should go through THO/terminology governance.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive OO issue asking to clarify the ReferenceRange meaning code `normal` definition from an imprecise 95th-percentile statement to wording based on two standard deviations and 95.45% of the relevant control population.
initial_application: Commit 1e59a65e1b6dc1798196f55d782d17e3400b1355 (`GF#16139`) changed the then-core `source/observation/codesystem-referencerange-meaning.xml` `normal` concept definition to the two-standard-deviation/95.45% wording.
additional_context: FHIR-19772 later relaxed the same definition so the statistical rule is described as typical rather than mandatory; that issue was pre-applied in f103fbd30441a7596bc298842427ef0fdf1be564 and already audited on the combined branch in 7bd090c2d0111946a038368a15583db2cc91eaf9. Commit 5c0494aacfd0b8bd52bc72c587aa89d0a64246f8 then removed the core CodeSystem source during the UTG/THO migration, leaving current core to reference THO through `ValueSet/referencerange-meaning`.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Current FHIR core source binds Observation and ObservationDefinition elements to the ReferenceRange meaning ValueSet, and the maintained THO CodeSystem already contains the accepted refined `normal` definition.

related_jiras.note: Same ReferenceRange meaning code definition was relaxed after OO/Zulip discussion; it supersedes the strict FHIR-16139 wording and is already represented on the combined branch.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive OO issue requested clarification of the ReferenceRange meaning code `normal` definition from an imprecise 95th-percentile statement.

evidence_items.summary: Commit `GF#16139` changed the then-core CodeSystem source from the old 95th-percentile definition to the two-standard-deviation/95.45% definition.
